release_notes_md:
## Hotfix for v0.1.31

Fixes a SUP-gate and write-gate false-unblock caught during integration
testing on the lab VM.

### Bug

On any deployment that still carries a legacy `system_config[license_blob]`
row alongside the v0.1.26+ stackable `licenses` table (every existing
deployment), the Phase 3B SUP-gate and Phase 3G write-gate could be
falsely unblocked. The cross-worker coherence path in `check_can_update`
and `check_writes_allowed` read the legacy single-blob row instead of
the stackable aggregate. When the legacy row's SUP date differed from
the stackable aggregate's (e.g. after install/remove of stackable
licenses), the legacy reading won.

Result on lab VM: install of a lapsed-SUP license + removal of originals
left the stackable aggregate at `valid_support_lapsed`, but the legacy
row was unchanged and reported `valid` with future SUP — the SUP-gate
returned `None` (allowed) for every minor/major upgrade attempt.

### Fix

Swap `reverify_cached_blob` → `get_aggregated_state` in both gate
helpers. The aggregate is the stackable-licensing source of truth on
v0.1.26+ and has its own cross-worker coherence via the
`_active_set_fingerprint` md5 over the licenses table.

### Impact

Any v0.1.31 deployment relying on the SUP-gate or write-gate to block
unauthorized operations was effectively unprotected. Patch + minor +
major upgrades all unblocked; portal mutations on expired-demo
unblocked. Phase 3A band policy, cleanup worker, and Phase 3F worker
event-dropping are unaffected — they don't go through the bugged
paths.

### Test coverage

Updated the original unit tests, which had been mocking the wrong
helper (the very layer that caused the bug). Now mock
`get_aggregated_state` instead. Suite stays at 401 passing.
